analysis.title: Fixed Income Weekly Update (October 27th, 2026)
key_insights: U.S. Treasuries posted a third consecutive weekly gain. Mounting global and domestic risks outweighed renewed energy-driven inflation concerns.
Early-week losses reflected firm oil prices and a poorly received 20-year bond auction. Disappointing housing starts and a plunge in pending home sales reinforced concerns about economic momentum.

The decisive rally came Thursday on renewed stress in French sovereign debt, escalating Middle East uncertainty and continued weakness among highly leveraged AI infrastructure companies, which drove safe-haven demand and short covering.
Yields briefly reached one-month lows before Friday's rebound in crude oil and cautious positioning ahead of the Fed meeting triggered profit-taking.
For the week the 2-year yield fell about 3 bp to 4.68%, the 10-year fell 8 bp to 5.00% and the 30-year fell 10 bp to 5.32%. The curve bull flattened, with 2s/10s at 0.31%, down 5.4 bp.

U.S. crude oil inventories including the SPR fell to 695 million barrels, the lowest since 1983. Less capacity to absorb supply disruptions raises the risk of oil price spikes, which could fuel inflation and weaken growth.
Next week's calendar centers on Fed, ECB and BOJ rate decisions, advance Q3 GDP and September PCE inflation. Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon report earnings.

Arguments for a Treasury selloff: WTI above $103, October flash PMI selling prices rising at the fastest pace since August 2022, composite PMI at 57.6, 82% of reporting S&P 500 companies beating earnings, initial claims at 194k, and $183 billion of 2-, 5- and 7-year auctions next week.

Arguments for a Treasury rally: French 10-year yields above 5% with the spread over Bunds the widest since 2011, record Meta CDS spreads and credit pressure on Oracle and other AI borrowers, September pending home sales down 7.3% to the lowest since records began in 2001, and Atlanta Fed business inflation expectations easing to 2.3%.
Survey expectations for the week: core PCE 3.10% y/y vs 3.0% prior, Q3 GDP 3.2% annualized vs 2.2% prior, FOMC target upper bound 4.00% per the Oct survey.
earnings_insights: 82% of reporting S&P 500 companies have exceeded earnings expectations so far this season (reported).
Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon are scheduled to report results in the coming week.
